comparisons.peer_topic: Year-over-Year Provision for Credit Losses Analysis
comparisons.peer_summary: Provision for credit losses increased to $1.35 billion in 2024 from $1.03 billion in 2023. The 2024 increase was primarily driven by net charge-offs in the credit card portfolio, while 2023 provisions included credit card charge-offs and wholesale loan impairments, partially offset by reserve reductions related to the GreenSky and Marcus portfolio transactions.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Goldman Sachs reported an increase in provision for credit losses in 2024 compared to 2023. Citigroup's provision increased to $463 million, driven by $168 million in net credit losses. Goldman Sachs saw a larger increase, with provisions rising to $1.35 billion from $1.03 billion, primarily driven by net charge-offs in the credit card portfolio. Unlike Citigroup's emphasis on spread products, Goldman Sachs highlighted credit card portfolios as the main driver, while also noting reserve reductions in 2023 related to GreenSky and Marcus portfolio transactions that did not recur in 2024.
